title: Rewrite weight manifest prober and tokenizer demarcation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Over the last 18 months multiple ad-hoc manifest variants and heuristic token-boundary detectors accumulated in the ingest stack. This causes intermittent boot latency regressions and unpredictable tokenizer failures for corner-case checkpoints. Goal: Replace the brittle manifest-probing heuristics with an explicit probe+schema negotiator, add a deterministic tokenizer demarcation step, and provide a non-destructive migration tool to normalize legacy manifests. This should reduce cold-start variance, make shard activation deterministic across streaming and lazy-load paths, and simplify downstream runtime kernel selection.
acceptance_criteria: New manifest prober returns schema id and a stable field map for all known public checkpoint formats
Token boundary demarcation passes existing tokenizer regression suite and reduces tokenizer mismatch rate to <0.1% on synthetic corpus
A migration CLI (manifest-mender) can convert legacy manifests to schema-v2 without changing weight blobs
End-to-end boot time for a 30B multi-shard model (cold start) improves p50 by >=20% in CI benchmarks
No regression on existing canary fleet for 2 weeks post-rollout
notes: Design: Introduce a two-phase prober: lightweight header probe (fast path) + content fingerprint probe (fallback). The prober emits canonical schema ids instead of ad-hoc flags.

Tokenizer demarcation: shift from heuristic split on embedding offsets to deterministic 'token-range' descriptor written into manifest; runtime will use descriptor to initialize tokenizer bridge state.
Migration strategy: manifest-mender will write .manifest.v2 next to original manifest and support a --dry-run mode for audits.
Compatibility: runtime will support both v1 and v2 manifests for 90 days; prober flags will surface when a v1 is seen and trigger background conversion jobs for Dedicated customers (opt-in).
Perf tradeoffs: header probe is minimal overhead; fingerprint probe will use sampled mmap reads capped at 128KB to avoid IO amplification on large shards.
Edge case: sharded checkpoints with non-uniform chunk ordering require shard-coordinator remap table; we'll add remap table generation to manifest-mender.
comments: 2025-02-19 - Aisha Patel: Kicked off design doc and shared initial sequence diagram in Confluence. Noted failure mode when tokenizer config file is missing in older manifests.
2025-02-24 - Miguel Ortega: Spike completed — header probe + sample-fingerprint proof-of-concept. Measured false-negative rate 1.3% on legacy corpus. Need extra entropy in fingerprint to hit <0.5%.
2025-02-27 - Design review (PM + Runtime): Agreed to keep v1 reads for 90-day compatibility window. PM requested migration opt-in for Dedicated customers to avoid surprises.
2025-03-03 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/1428 implementing prober and manifest-mender skeleton. Requesting initial review from @sophia and @jiawei.
2025-03-05 - Perf: CI synthetic benchmark (30B, 4 shards) shows cold-start p50 1.6s down from 2.0s baseline on x86-ampere. Multi-gpu shard activation ordering looks stable in 30/30 runs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Merge feature flag gated prober to main behind feature flag ingest.prober_v2 and run on internal canary fleet for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (migration): Run manifest-mender as dry-run on all hosted manifests, collect conversion metrics and remap failure list
Phase 3 (opt-in conversion): Offer Dedicated customers a migration window and provide conversion plan with support engineers
Phase 4 (flip): After 2 weeks stable, enable prober_v2 by default and start background conversions for v1 manifests with low-priority throttled jobs
Phase 5 (cleanup): Deprecate v1 readers after 90 days and remove legacy prober code in the next minor release
